reviewedProjects.name: GameSync Capability Truth / UI QoL
reviewedProjects.fact: GameSync Next already has a machine-readable parity matrix with verified, implemented-unverified, and gap states plus an executable audit that checks evidence semantics and concrete source/build invariants.
reviewedProjects.proposal: Generate a read-only Capability Truth surface directly from the parity matrix/audit output. Include evidence/test gates, source watermarks, stale-verification detection, exact destinations, and filters for gap/unverified/stale/verified states. The UI must never promote itself to verified.
reviewedProjects.benefit: Eliminates duplicate truth databases and makes UI claims traceable to source/test/runtime evidence.
reviewedProjects.risk: A second manually maintained status store would drift; stale historical verification could be misrepresented as current proof.
reviewedProjects.migration: Add a generator/view over the existing parity contract; do not replace the matrix or audit.
reviewedProjects.experiment: Render one-to-one matrix rows and assert exact status/evidence counts against the audit result on the current GameSync source watermarks.
reviewedProjects.acceptance: Every displayed capability maps to one canonical matrix record, status counts match the audit, stale source changes are flagged, filters are non-mutating, and verification cannot be escalated by the presentation layer.

reviewedProjects.name: GameSync Release Factory
reviewedProjects.fact: GitHub artifact attestations use Sigstore-backed provenance, and GitHub release-asset metadata exposes a digest field that can carry SHA-256 identity.
reviewedProjects.proposal: Add GitHub-native artifact attestation and release-asset digest verification after GameSync's existing internal manifest/hash/fresh-extraction gates. Keep internal deterministic verification as the first authority rather than outsourcing correctness to GitHub metadata.
reviewedProjects.benefit: Adds independently verifiable provenance and stronger remote release identity without weakening current packaging verification.
reviewedProjects.risk: Treating a successful upload/attestation as proof of runtime correctness would weaken the release gate.
reviewedProjects.migration: Generate deterministic internal release evidence first, then attach/verify provenance for the exact already-verified bytes.
reviewedProjects.experiment: Attest one non-production release candidate and verify local SHA-256 equals internal manifest, GitHub release digest, and attestation subject before any promotion.
reviewedProjects.acceptance: All three identities agree, fresh extraction still passes, no existing release path is removed, and rollback metadata remains complete.

reviewedProjects.name: GameSync Bounty / Rewards Runtime
reviewedProjects.fact: Twitch's Get Drops Entitlements API is an organization/game-owner integration surface, not a general viewer-side source of truth that can replace all user-session reward evidence.
reviewedProjects.proposal: Keep GameSync's proof collectors and ready-to-claim versus externally-claimed distinction. Add provider-specific entitlement adapters only where the authenticated provider contract actually grants the required authority.
reviewedProjects.benefit: Prevents false reward claims and avoids forcing an incompatible server-side entitlement API into end-user browser flows.
reviewedProjects.risk: Conflating browser-observed progress, provider entitlement, and external claim completion would corrupt the reward ledger.
reviewedProjects.migration: Preserve the deterministic local ledger and add explicit provider evidence classes rather than a generic claimed boolean.
reviewedProjects.experiment: Create fixtures for manual proof, browser-session watch evidence, provider entitlement evidence, and external claim acknowledgement with contradictory/missing combinations.
reviewedProjects.acceptance: The runtime never marks externally claimed without authoritative acknowledgement, preserves BigInt-safe deterministic state, and distinguishes unsupported provider evidence visibly.

reviewedProjects.name: GameSync Source Finder / Entity Resolver
reviewedProjects.fact: Current candidate remote search engines include Typesense 30.2 and Meilisearch 1.53.1, while SQLite FTS5 remains a capable local full-text primitive. Shipping GameSync already isolates remote search behind a normalized Typesense/Meilisearch client and uses FlexSearch locally.
reviewedProjects.proposal: Run a backend-neutral Search Backend Arena on the existing labeled game/mod/entity corpus instead of migrating because one backend is newer. Compare current local behavior, SQLite FTS5, Typesense 30.2, and Meilisearch 1.53.1.
reviewedProjects.benefit: Selects search technology by real entity-resolution accuracy, source provenance, latency, and offline behavior while preserving backend portability.
reviewedProjects.risk: Semantic/vector improvements can increase false merges, which is worse than a missed match for project identity.
reviewedProjects.migration: Keep the normalized adapter boundary and replace/add a backend only after corpus-based evidence proves a material advantage.
reviewedProjects.experiment: Measure top-k recall, false-merge rate, latency, explainability/provenance, offline behavior, index size, and update cost on the identical labeled corpus.
reviewedProjects.acceptance: Any adopted backend materially improves useful recall/latency without increasing false merges or weakening exact identity/source evidence.

reviewedProjects.name: GameSync Script Polling Runtime
reviewedProjects.fact: Chrome documents that extension alarms may be cleared on browser restart and recommends checking/recreating required alarms whenever the service worker starts. Current Chrome also supports a persistAcrossSessions alarm option on newer versions, while service-worker termination/restart is normal lifecycle behavior.
reviewedProjects.proposal: Persist scheduler intent, check/recreate the scriptTrackerPoll alarm during service-worker startup, feature-detect persistAcrossSessions where supported, and keep ScriptDb due-times as the canonical catch-up truth after restart.
reviewedProjects.benefit: Makes polling resilient to service-worker/browser restarts without increasing poll frequency or losing due work.
reviewedProjects.risk: Blindly recreating alarms can duplicate scheduling; trusting only alarm persistence can miss overdue scripts after restart.
reviewedProjects.migration: Add idempotent ensure-alarm startup logic around the existing ScriptPollScheduler and preserve current due-time/jitter logic.
reviewedProjects.experiment: In an isolated extension build, schedule mixed due/future scripts, terminate/restart the service worker/browser, verify a single alarm exists, and confirm overdue work catches up exactly once.
reviewedProjects.acceptance: No duplicate alarm/listener, no lost overdue checks, no reduced provider/script coverage, current scheduling heuristics remain intact, and restart behavior passes in the real supported browser runtime.

projectConstellationImprovement.name: Capability Truth Lens
projectConstellationImprovement.description: Add a read-only Project Constellation lens that summarizes canonical capability gaps, implemented-unverified items, stale verification, and verified items from project-owned evidence without allowing the second-brain UI to mutate verification authority.
projectConstellationImprovement.antiDegradation: The lens is additive, never hides canonical records, never changes capability status, and does not replace the dependency-free Quick View recovery surface.
projectConstellationImprovement.acceptance: Lens counts and links are generated from project-owned truth sources, stale evidence is visible, clearing/filtering the lens changes no project data, and all exact-destination links land on the promised source/evidence.
